test_title: SSC Selection Post Matric Level Official Paper (Held On: 27 June, 2023 Shift 1)
subject: general
question: A grocer sells pulses at a profit of 13% and uses weights which are 24% less than the market weight. The percentage of profit (correct to 2 decimal places) earned by him will be:
solution:
Given:

A grocer sells pulses at 13% profit and uses weights which are 24% less than the market weight

Formula used:

SP = CP(1 + P%)

P% = [(SP - CP)/CP] × 100

Calculations:

Let the CP of rice be x

⇒ SP = x(1 + 13%)

⇒ SP = x(1 + 0.13)

⇒ SP = 1.13x

Faulty weights are 24% less than market ones than

Actual weight of 1 kg weight = 1000 - 240 = 760 gm

Now SP of 720gm of rice is 1.13x then

⇒ SP of 1gm of rice = 1.13x/760

⇒ SP of 1000gm rice = 1130x/760 = 1.569x

Now P% = [(1.486x - x)/x] × 100

⇒ P% = [0.486x/x] × 100

⇒ P% = 0.486 × 100 = 48.6%

∴ The total gain earned by him is 48.68%.

⇒ 1st case, Profit% = 13%

⇒ 2nd case, Profit% = 24%

∴ (S.P/C.P) = (113/100) × (100/76) = 113/76

so, 

⇒ S.P = 113x and C.P = 76x

⇒ Profit = (113x - 76x) = 37x

∴ Overall Profit% = (37x)/(76x) × 100 = 48.68%.
